feedback.problem:
What is the Laplace transform of $f(t)={e}^{-3\text{i}t/8},$ where $t,s\in R?$$\,L(f(t))=$
{{field-1}},
defined for {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}f(t)\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

For the function $f(t)={e}^{-3\text{i}t/8},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}{e}^{-3\text{i}t/8}\text{d}t={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)t}\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating in the usual way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)t}\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)t}\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{(\frac{1}{-3\text{i}/8-s}{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)t})|}_{0}^{a} \\  & =\frac{1}{-3\text{i}/8-s}({lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)a}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}(1-{lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{(-3\text{i}/8-s)a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}-\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}({lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{-sa}\cdot {e}^{-3\text{i}a/8}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we recall Euler's formula:

$$
{e}^{\text{i}\theta }=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
F(s)=\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}-\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}[{lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{-sa}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3a/8)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3a/8))].
$$

Now, we have the following cases:

- For $s<0,$ the term ${e}^{-sa}$ increases without bound while $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3a/8)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3a/8)$ oscillates rapidly as $a\to \infty .$ Therefore, the limit does not exist for $s<0.$

- For $s=0,$ we have simply $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3a/8)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3a/8),$ which oscillates rapidly as $a\to \infty .$ Therefore, the limit does not exist for $s=0.$

- For $s>0,$ the term ${e}^{-sa}$ decays to zero while $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3a/8)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3a/8)$ oscillates rapidly as $a\to \infty .$ Therefore, the limit of their product equals zero.

Therefore, for $s>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & =\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}-\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}[{lim}_{a\to \infty }{e}^{-sa}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3a/8)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3a/8))] \\  & =\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{s+3\text{i}/8} \\  & =\frac{8}{8s+3\text{i}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Laplace transform of ${e}^{-3\text{i}t/8}$ is $F(s)=\frac{8}{8s+3\text{i}},$ defined for $s>0.$
